headlines.title: 5 Payment Stocks That Earn a Fee Every Time You Swipe
headlines.summary: Each of these businesses gets paid when you pay. Why does the market price some of those fees at around three times the rest?

headlines.title: Hamilton Wins Kansas Senate Race. Why It Matters For Credit Card Companies.
headlines.summary: Democrat Adam Hamilton has defeated incumbent Republican Sen. Roger Marshall in the Kansas senate race, according to the AP.

headlines.title: Visa Just Hiked Its Dividend by More Than 16%, But Investors Should Consider Waiting for V to Pull Back Before Buying.
headlines.summary: Visa raised its quarterly dividend by 16.4% to $0.78 per share after Q4 revenue rose 13% to $12.1 billion.

headlines.title: 4 Companies Just Raised Their Dividends. Which Payout Has the Most Room to Grow?
headlines.summary: Visa, Entergy, Tennant, and Fortis all just lifted their quarterly payouts, but a dividend raise is only as good as the cash flow standing behind it. One of these four companies raised its payout while its earnings coverage was already running thin.

headlines.title: Ackman calls stock market "broken" but touts Visa, MasterCard and Netflix
headlines.summary: Investing.com -- Bill Ackman expressed concern on Tuesday about the current state of the stock market, stating that increased speculative trading has created excessive price volatility driven by high levels of leverage.

description: Visa Inc. operates as a payment technology company in the United States and internationally. The company operates VisaNet, a transaction processing network that enables authorization, clearing, and settlement of payment transactions. It also offers credit, debit, and prepaid card products; tap to pay, tokenization, and click to pay services; Visa Direct, a platform which facilitates money movement, enabling clients to collect, hold, convert, and send funds across its network; and issuing solutions, such as airport lounge access, dining reservations, shopping experiences, event tickets, and seller offers. In addition, the company provides acceptance solutions, an omnichannel payment integration with e-commerce platforms; risk detection and prevention solutions; and advisory and other services comprising consulting practice, proprietary analytics models, data scientists and economists, marketing services, and managed services. It provides its services under the Visa, Visa Electron, V PAY, Interlink, and PLUS brands. The company serves consumers, sellers, financial institutions, and government entities. Visa Inc. was founded in 1958 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California.
